firstLossStatement: The failure is not a wrong value anywhere in the chain — it is a MISSING SAMPLE. The layout probe samples [390, 768, 1024, 1440, 1920]. The source's real breakpoint for the pricing comparison table is 1025px, which falls in the unsampled gap (1024, 1440). Every downstream stage is faithful to the samples it was given: the observation correctly records hidden@1024 / visible@1440, the SiteSpec carries that verbatim, and the reconstruction then INFERS the boundary at the arithmetic midpoint 1232. The inference is where the defect becomes VISIBLE (materializationStage), but the information that would have placed the boundary at 1025 was already absent from the pipeline at the observation stage.
materializationStatement: src/reconstruction/layout-inference.ts hiddenRanges() converts hidden probe widths into an @media band by flooring the midpoint between the last hidden and the first visible sample: floor((1024+1440)/2) = 1232, minus 0.02 => (min-width: 1024px) and (max-width: 1231.98px). The band overshoots the true 1025px boundary by 207px on the upper edge and undershoots it by 109px on the lower edge (the band starts at 1024, but the desktop variant becomes active at 915).

creatingCodePath.summary: One function, one arithmetic convention. hiddenRanges() in the layout inference turns the probe's hidden-width set into an @media band by flooring the midpoint between adjacent samples. With samples {1024 hidden, 1440 visible} the midpoint is 1232, so the band runs 1024..1231.98 — 207px past the source's real 1025px boundary.

chain.role: defines the sample grid the whole inference is built on
chain.why: No sample between 1024 and 1440. The source's pricing breakpoint (1025) and the whole 'laptop' band live inside that gap, so no measurement downstream can see them.

chain.code: const desktopIdx = widths.map((width, i) => ({ width, i })).filter((entry) => entry.width >= input.breakpoint);
chain.why: breakpoint is 915 (the inferred mobile/desktop switch), so desktopIdx = [1024, 1440, 1920] — three samples spanning 896px of viewport range.
n000359 is visible at the truth width (1440) and hidden at 1024, so it qualifies. Evidence string stored on the rule: 'visible at 1440px, hidden at 1024px'.

chain.role: THE RULE-CREATING LINE — computes the band bounds
chain.code:
start = previous ? Math.floor((previous.width + entry.width) / 2) : entry.width;   // line 674
const boundary = Math.floor((sorted[i - 1]!.width + entry.width) / 2);            // line 677
ranges.push(`(min-width: ${start}px) and (max-width: ${boundary - 0.02}px)`);      // line 678
chain.arithmetic: sorted desktop = [1024(hidden), 1440(visible), 1920(visible)]. i=0: hidden, no previous sample inside desktopIdx, so start = 1024 (the sample width itself, NOT a midpoint). i=1: visible, boundary = floor((1024 + 1440) / 2) = 1232. Emitted: (min-width: 1024px) and (max-width: 1231.98px).
chain.why: The midpoint convention is a reasonable default when samples are dense; here the adjacent samples are 416px apart, so the midpoint is a 208px-wide guess in each direction. The upper edge lands 207px past the truth. The lower edge is worse-shaped than a midpoint: because 1024 is the FIRST desktop sample, the `previous ? ... : entry.width` fallback pins the band's start to 1024 exactly, leaving 915..1023.98 uncovered — a stretch where the desktop variant is live but the hide band is not, so the clone SHOWS the table the source hides.

chain.role: renders the rule text into the shipped sheet
chain.why: One @media block per node at specificity (0,3,0) so it outranks the exact-style class. 738 such blocks ship; 503 of them are on p000007.

chain.role: the gate that does not gate
chain.code:
isResponsiveHidden = rule.kind === "responsive-hidden" && rule.media !== undefined;  // line 107
// documented: "What it deliberately does NOT check: `responsive-hidden` rules ... They are accepted unchecked and counted separately (`acceptedUnchecked`)."
chain.why: The truth check re-renders only at the truth width (1440). A band that by construction cannot match at 1440 is unfalsifiable there, so every responsive-hidden rule ships unverified BY DESIGN. Nothing in the pipeline ever renders at a width inside the band and compares against the source, which is why a 207px overshoot on the most content-dense page in the site survived to release.

creatingCodePath.rootCauseOneLine: A 5-point probe grid with a 416px hole between 1024 and 1440, plus a midpoint interpolation that ships unverified because the only verification width (1440) lies outside every band it produces.

notes: Nothing under src/ was modified. No git operation was run. data/ was read only.
Reproduces the 28.5B pricingTableProbe exactly: clone 2348 vs source 2634 visible chars at 1100 (28.5B measured 2351 vs 2637 — same defect, same magnitude, 3-char drift from live-source churn).

The band's LOWER edge is also wrong, in the opposite direction: between 915 and 1023.98 the clone shows the comparison table (visibleTextChars 2672 at 950/1000/1023) while the source hides it (max-width:1024). 28.5B concluded 'the band's lower edge is right' from the 914/1024 sample pair; that pair straddles the error rather than bracketing it. Any fix must move BOTH edges to 1025, not just the upper one.

responsive-hidden rules ship unverified by documented design (layout-truth-check.ts:46-51). Widening the probe grid without adding an in-band verification width would only move the guess, not prove it.
